hints: Think about what you actually see and feel when anhydrous aluminium chloride meets water, is it quiet and cooling or vigorous and heating?
Remember that $\text{Al}^{3+}$ is small and highly charged, so consider what its hexaaqua ion does to water molecules around it.
Link the formation of the hydrated aluminium ion to the release of $\text{H}^+$ ions to decide which two statements fit together.
walkthrough:
**Observe the reaction with water**

Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ reacts vigorously with water with lots of fumes and heat released. That tells us the hydration and hydrolysis is strongly exothermic, not endothermic.

So statement 1 is false: $$\text{AlCl}_3(s) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^- \quad \Delta H < 0$$

**Identify the aluminium species in dilute solution**

In plenty of water, the $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ion is fully hydrated to form the octahedral hexaaquaaluminium(III) ion. This is the stable form in a 0.1 mol dm$^{-3}$ solution.

So statement 3 is true: $$\text{Al}^{3+} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$$

**Explain the acidity by hydrolysis**

The $[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ ion has very high charge density. It polarises and weakens O-H bonds in the attached water ligands, so a proton is donated to water.

$$[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{OH})]^{2+} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$
This release of $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ makes the solution acidic with pH around 3, so statement 2 is true.

**Combine the true statements**

Statement 1 is false, statements 2 and 3 are true. That combination corresponds to 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes statement 1. The reaction of anhydrous AlCl3 with water is famously vigorous and exothermic, with steamy HCl fumes, not endothermic.
options.B: Incorrect because it pairs 1 and 2 only. While statement 2 is true (the solution is acidic), statement 1 is false and statement 3 is missing. The hexaaqua ion is definitely present.
options.C: Correct because only 2 and 3 are true. Dilute solution contains [Al(H2O)6]3+ which undergoes hydrolysis to release H3O+, giving an acidic solution. Statement 1 is false as the process is exothermic.
options.D: Incorrect because it selects statement 1 only. Statement 1 is the false one, and it ignores the two true observations about acidity and the hexaaqua complex.
